pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

content.text:
I found two spec defects and three smaller fixes. The `test` script in package.json does not work on Node 22, and an invalid `PORT` containing a newline makes the server write two lines to stderr.

**Spec defects**
1. **The `test` script fails** (/root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/package.json:9). `node --test test/` fails on Node v22.23.4. When I ran `node --test .smoke/`, it stopped with `Cannot find module '/root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/.smoke'`. Passing the file path ran 4 of 4 tests. Node 22 reads `--test` arguments as file names or glob patterns, not folders. So `npm test` will fail even with a good test suite, which breaks "Project's own tests must pass".
2. **The PORT error can be more than one line** (/root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/server.mjs:325). `fail(\`invalid PORT ${process.env.PORT}\`)` prints the raw value. For `PORT=$'1\n2'`, the digit regex rejects it correctly, but the message then spans two lines. The spec asks for "one line of its choice".

**Smaller issues**
- **Save is not atomic** (server.mjs:132-133). `writeFile` writes straight over the data file. If a write fails partway (for example ENOSPC), memory stays unchanged, but the file is left cut short and the next start fails. The spec says a failed save changes nothing. Writing a temp file in the same folder and then renaming it fixes this without creating folders.
- **Errors are dropped silently** (server.mjs:297, 302, 304). `res.on('error', () => {})` has a comment explaining it. The `.catch(() => res.destroy())` drops any unexpected error with no trace. Writing one line to stderr is allowed after startup, because only stdout is limited to the listening line.
- **`createApp` is too long** (server.mjs:194-272). At 79 lines it breaks the under-50 rule. It holds state, three handlers, commit, page serving and routing. Moving routing (lines 242-269) out into its own function would fix it.
- **Small cleanups.** In the `clientError` handler (server.mjs:332-333), `err` is unused and sockets have no `headersSent` property, so that test does nothing. Also, `deleteBooking` (server.mjs:223) turns ids longer than 2^53 into the wrong number. That is harmless in practice.

**What I checked that is correct**
- Startup order (PORT, then data file, then listen) and the exit codes.
- Default port 3000, the digit check and the 65535 upper limit.
- The exact listening line and its port.
- `DATA_FILE` defaults, cwd resolution, the exact `<name>` and the error text.
- ENOENT on read means no bookings, and the stored layout is checked strictly.
- Memory changes only after a successful save, with 500 `internal error` on failure.
- Requests are handled one at a time through a single queue.
- The whole body is read before any reply, and 413 counts every byte received.
- Booking rules 1-10 run in order, and every message string is exact.
- 409 reports the overlapping booking that starts earliest.
- Routes match the raw path up to `?`, the query is parsed with URLSearchParams, and `params.has('date')` / `params.get('date')` behave as specified.
- The 405-before-404 order is right, including `GET /api/bookings/abc` and HEAD on pages.
- The pages are served with the correct Content-Types, `Object.hasOwn` guards the page lookup, and JSON content types and the empty 204 body are correct.
- `toString('utf8')` keeps the byte order mark, as the spec requires.

I could not run the startup edge cases (newline in PORT, port too large, data file that is a directory) because Bash permission was denied, so those points come from reading the code.

## GRADE
Overall: 7/10
Verdict: fail
structure: 8 — clear sections, frozen state replaced on each commit, single serialising queue; createApp mixes routing with state handling
naming: 8 — descriptive and consistent (MSG, isValidLayout, commit); `q`/`only` are terse
duplication: 9 — validators shared between API and data-file check; no copy-paste
size: 7 — file 343 lines is fine, but createApp is 79 lines (over the 50-line limit)
errors: 7 — err.code, exact messages and exit codes are right, but an invalid PORT can produce a multi-line stderr message, the non-atomic save can corrupt the data file, and unexpected errors are dropped silently
tests: n/a — written by the testing section
security: 9 — no secrets, raw paths matched exactly, hasOwn guard, body size capped
leftovers: 9 — no console.log or debug code; unused `err` param in clientError
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/package.json:9 change `"node --test test/"` to `"node --test \"test/**/*.test.mjs\""` (Node 22 does not accept a folder argument here, so `npm test` fails)
- /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/server.mjs:325 do not print the raw PORT (or print `JSON.stringify(process.env.PORT)`) so the stderr message stays one line
- /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/server.mjs:132 write to a temp file in the same folder (e.g. `${filePath}.tmp`), then `fs.promises.rename` it over the data file, so a failed save leaves the old file intact
- /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/server.mjs:302 write one line to stderr for an unexpected error before `res.destroy()` instead of dropping it
- /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/server.mjs:194 split createApp: move `route` (lines 242-269) out into its own function that takes the handlers, so every function is under 50 lines
- /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/server.mjs:332 drop the unused `err` param and the `socket.headersSent` check (sockets have no such property)
